learning_outcomes.text: Understand the concept of the electromagnetic environment, the functional coexistence of electronic devices, and the nature of interference between devices and systems, both electrical and electronic.
Explore and deepen understanding of electromagnetic interference (EMI) emissions and immunity to environmental interference.
Examine the risks associated with conducted and radiated emissions from devices, focusing on their potential impact on both equipment and individuals exposed in occupational settings.
Learn to distinguish between direct risks, stemming from exposure to electromagnetic fields, and indirect risks, related to interference affecting equipment critical to human safety.
Provide an overview of the main international and national standards on electromagnetic compatibility (EMC) and safety, along with the methodologies for measurement and compliance verification.
Identify in realistic situations the emission responsible, the victim and the coupling mechanism of the interference capable of degrading the performance of the apparatus or system under examination.

Apply the knowledge to the analysis of potentially dangerous situations even for the operators who use the equipment, with the ability to formulate possible mitigation solutions both in terms of filtering and shielding of electromagnetic interference.
Identify and define specific risk measurement and assessment techniques and procedures.
Improve learning capability through a global approach and synthesis effort.
Improve communication and interaction skills through opinion sharing and team working methodology during the study of real-life cases.

syllabus_topics: Conducted and radiated propagation and coupling mechanisms
Emission and susceptibility of electronic analog and digital equipment for communication, industrial and power applications
Direct safety due to human exposure to intentional and non-intentional sources
Indirect safety due to electromagnetic susceptibility of equipments
National and international standards for electromagnetic compatibility and safety assessment
Instrumentation for electromagnetic interference and human exposure measurements
Shielding actions: passive and active shielding
Laboratory lessons in front of typical test benches adopted for compatibility and safety assessment
Narrowband measurements of emissions and human exposure to em fields
Broadband measurements of emissions and human exposure to em fields

assessment_methods.method: Written answers for calculation, diagrams, schemes, graphics, analytical demonstrations during oral examination
Written report on real cases (optional, if required)

assessment_rules: The examination is oral and consists of three questions about all topics. Questions requiring calculation, drawing, or analytical demonstrations will be answered in written form during the oral examination. A written report on real cases may be required and used for one question. Each question is scored from zero to ten, summed for a total in thirtieths. The examination is passed if the total score is 18/30 or greater. "30/30 with distinction" is awarded for strong ability and autonomy in theoretical demonstrations in addition to correct and complete answers.
